findings.failure_scenario: A machine whose maind state is still ~/.maind (agents.json, memory-backups/, and, when that file was the active fleet source, registry.json) has no <state>/maind directory and no ~/.swissknifeman/topology.json. maind topology init (or the skiller topology alias) calls save_topology, which mkdir's the parent of <state>/maind/topology.json. Env.state_dir then resolves to that new directory because it exists. The next maind process reads <state>/maind/agents.json and <state>/maind/registry.json, which were never written, so maind agents shows an empty registry and a fleet that lived only in ~/.maind/registry.json disappears. The files remain under ~/.maind. No warning is printed on the switch. Phase rule 5 forbids a silent move: the legacy directory stays active until the new place already exists.
findings.reproduction: In a temporary HOME with SKM_HOME unset, resolve_with_legacy(state_dir('maind'), [~/.maind]) returned ~/.maind while registry.json and agents.json were files there. After Path(state_dir('maind')/'topology.json').parent.mkdir, the same call returned <state>/maind. Those two files were not present in the new directory and were still present under ~/.maind.

triage_reproduction.cmd: HOME=$T/h (with ~/.maind/{registry,agents}.json, SKM_HOME unset) python3: Env(...).state_dir; topology.save_topology(env, {...}); Env(...).state_dir; registry_file.exists()
triage_reproduction.observed: before: ~/.maind; after save_topology: ~/.local/state/swissknifeman/maind; registry_file.exists() False while ~/.maind/registry.json still exists, so the fleet registry silently disappears from the active state dir

findings.failure_scenario: A home with neither <state>/skiller/projects.json nor ~/.swissknifeman/projects.json runs packages/skiller/install.sh. Lines 95–97 mkdir ~/.swissknifeman and write an empty projects.json there. Env.db_file then calls resolve_with_legacy, sees that legacy file, and keeps it as the write target. skiller connect stores the project only in ~/.swissknifeman/projects.json; <state>/skiller/projects.json is never created. The registry the contract places in aicore.state stays unused for every install that seeds the old file.
findings.reproduction: Not executed. Read install.sh:95–97 and common.py:46–52 against aicore.state.resolve_with_legacy (legacy exists and the new file does not → return the legacy path).

triage_reproduction.cmd: T=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p $T/.swissknifeman; printf '{"version":1,"projects":[]}' > $T/.swissknifeman/projects.json; HOME=$T PYTHONPATH=packages/aicore/lib:packages/skiller/lib python3 -c "import pathlib; from skiller.common import Env; print(Env(root=pathlib.Path('packages/skiller'),home=pathlib.Path('$T')).db_file)"
triage_reproduction.observed: prints $T/.swissknifeman/projects.json, with a legacy-location warning; the new <state>/skiller/projects.json is not used. install.sh:95-97 creates exactly that seeded legacy file when none exists.

findings.failure_scenario: A home with no ~/.swissknifeman/topology.json runs maind topology init. The map is written to <state>/maind/topology.json, or to ~/.maind/topology.json while that directory is still the active state dir. The memory hook's topo_node_path reads only $HOME/.swissknifeman/topology.json (MEM_TOPO, line 54) and returns empty, so brain, swissknifeman and projects_base fall through to the weak defaults. The same split hits the connected-project list: harness safe-dirs --all-projects (safedirs.py:179) and the auto-approve hook (auto-approve/lib/safedirs.py:81) open only ~/.swissknifeman/projects.json. After a connect on a machine that never had that file, the registry is at <state>/skiller/projects.json and those readers see no projects. Before this move, skiller topology init and the registry write were exactly the paths those readers open.
findings.reproduction: Not executed. Read maind/common.py:45–55 and topology.py:54–59 for the write path, and common.sh:54–66, safedirs.py:179, auto-approve/lib/safedirs.py:78–85 for the reads.

rejected.reason: The readers are in packages/harness (memory hook common.sh, harness safedirs.py, auto-approve hook safedirs.py). That is outside this item's write set, and the plan scopes the harness-side lookup change to the harness item, per hub-p11-harness. D70 also fixes the maind and skiller side as the new place with a legacy fallback. The legacy file stays readable and is not migrated until upgrade. The finding is a cross-module follow-up, not a defect of this item's contract.
